paper_metadata.title: Effect of Ageing on Microstructure, Mechanical Properties and Creep Behavior of Alloy 740H

evidence.quote: A study on the mechanical property changes and the creep behavior of a Ni-based alloy 740H
This as-received alloy will hitherto be referred to as ''AR'' alloy in this work.
The alloy subjected to ageing treatment will be hitherto referred to as ''aged'' alloy.

This alloy was manufactured by Vacuum Induction Melting (VIM) of raw materials and remelting of the ingot obtained from VIM process was performed, so as to ensure better chemical homogeneity, lower defects and lower inclusion content.

This alloy was manufactured by Vacuum Induction Melting (VIM) of raw materials and remelting of the ingot obtained from VIM process was performed, so as to ensure better chemical homogeneity, lower defects and lower inclusion content.

attributes.location: within grain and at grain boundaries

evidence.quote: MC and M23C6 carbides were observed within the grain as well as at the grain boundaries in the AR and aged condition of the alloy.

Higher magnification imaging reveals that M23C6 is present as discontinuous precipitates in AR alloy (see Figure 2(c)) but forms a continuous network like structure at the grain boundaries upon ageing (see Figure 2(d)).
In comparison, the average size of γ¢ in the aged alloy is ~ 253 nm, which indicates that γ¢ undergo significant coarsening during ageing.

Magnified images of the aged alloy in Figure 2(d) reveal a ~ 0.3 μm wide γ¢ precipitate-free zone near the grain boundaries.
